paragraphs.text: Which some render the lilies of the testimony, and interpret of the Jewish polity or commonwealth, called by Josephus θεοκρατεια, that is, a God-government. Kimchi saith that Shoshannim-Eduth is species toni nobis hodie ignota, a kind of musical strain not known to us today.
paragraphs.anchor: Upon Shoshannim-Eduth

paragraphs.text: Thou that feedest thy people, watchest over them, defendest, redeemest, reducest them; thou that handlest them, curest them, washest them, drivest them as they are able to go, carryest them in thy bosom, doest all the offices of a good shepherd for them. In calling upon God it is wisdom to make choice of fit appellations and attributes, such as may strengthen our faith and increase our fervour.
paragraphs.anchor: Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel

paragraphs.text: Joseph is named quia nobilis inter fratres, saith Austin; the first birthright was taken from Reuben, and given to Joseph, 1Ch 5:1, hence he is put for the whole people.
paragraphs.anchor: Thou that leadest Joseph

paragraphs.text: Thou that dwellest between (or sittest upon) the cherubims] Those winged creatures that covered the mercy seat, the ark, and the two tables of the law within it; and all, to set forth Christ covering the curses of the law, and graciously dwelling with the sons of men, to the admiration of angels.
Show thy power in saving thy people and punishing their enemies. Shine as the sun doth in his strength.
paragraphs.anchor: Shine forth

paragraphs.text: These three tribes went next after the ark, when it removed, Num 2:18-24; Num 10:22-24
paragraphs.anchor: Before Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasseh

paragraphs.text: Which seemeth at present to lie dormant.
paragraphs.anchor: Stir up thy strength

paragraphs.text: Turn again our captivity, or show thyself reconciled unto us in Christ, who is here called the face of God, as some conceive.
paragraphs.anchor: Turn us again

paragraphs.text: Iehova bellipotens Deus. God hath his upper and nether forces, as his horse and foot, ready pressed, say the Rabbis.
paragraphs.anchor: O Lord God of hosts

paragraphs.text: Heb. wilt thou smoke? As angry people seem to send out smoke at their nostrils.
paragraphs.anchor: How long wilt thou be angry

paragraphs.text: This is a sore affliction to the saints, that their prayers seem to be ineffectual.
paragraphs.anchor: Against the prayer of thy people

paragraphs.text: Panibus fletu intinctis (Chald.). It is as ordinary with them to weep as it is with men to eat and drink (Kimchi).
paragraphs.anchor: Thou feedest them with the bread of tears

paragraphs.text: Trientales they are Tricongii in a sense, to their sorrow. They are afflicted even to utmost satiety. See Psa 42:3. Holy Bradford oft mused at his meal, having his hat over his eyes, from whence came commonly plenty of tears dropping on his trencher (Acts aud Mon. 1457).
paragraphs.anchor: And givest them tears to drink in great measure

paragraphs.text: We have as many enemies as neighbours, all striving to enslave us. We are crushed between them as corn is between millstones.
paragraphs.anchor: Thou makest us a strife unto our neighbours

paragraphs.text: Make them merry in our misery, revel in our ruins.
paragraphs.anchor: And our enemies laugh among themselves

paragraphs.text: See Psa 80:3, and observe that there it was only, "Turn us again, O God," here, "O God of hosts," and Psa 80:19, "O Lord God of hosts." As the bird by much waving gathereth wind under the wing, and mounteth higher; so doth faith in prayer, viresque acquirit eundo.
paragraphs.anchor: Turn us again, O God of hosts

paragraphs.text: The Church is oft set forth by this similitude. The Rabbis say that Solomon made a vine of gold in the temple. Athenaeus telleth us that the kings of Persia sat under a golden vine having bunches of smaragds and other stately stones. All this was nothing to God’s vine, that plant of renown, brought out of Egypt (where it got no good, Eze 34:29; Eze 20:8), and set in a better soil.
paragraphs.anchor: Thou hast brought a vine out of Egypt

paragraphs.text: Espying out a fit place to plant it in, Eze 20:6, and making clean work before it, as some render the words ( Expurgasti coram ea), by pulling up those bad and barren weeds, the Canaanites, that might have hindered its growth.
paragraphs.anchor: Thou preparedst room before it

paragraphs.text: viz. By thy digging, dressing, watering, and mounding it; as of all possessions, none requireth greater care than that of vineyards, saith Care; and there is a peculiar affection in men toward the vine above all trees, as another observeth.
paragraphs.anchor: And didst cause it to take deep root

paragraphs.text: The Israelites grew amain in wealth, power, and multitude of men; witness their huge armies and valiant acts, though the country was not above 200 miles long, and 50 miles broad.
paragraphs.anchor: The hills were covered, &c.

paragraphs.text: The midland sea.
paragraphs.anchor: She sent out her boughs unto the sea

paragraphs.text: Euphrates. This was first done in David’s days.
paragraphs.anchor: And her branches unto the river

paragraphs.text: i.e. Taken away thy mighty hand hitherto held over her. This befell not till they degenerated into a strange vine, Jer 2:21, and brought forth wild grapes, Isa 5:4.
paragraphs.anchor: Why hast thou then broken down her hedges?

paragraphs.text: All swine (but wild ones especially) are vitibus inimici, saith Theodoret, destructions to vines. And Melancthon thinks that therefore God forbad the Jews to eat swine’s flesh, Eo quod sues omnia sursum deorsum vertant vastentque, because they turn up all, rooting things up by the roots, as the word here signifieth, Exvineavit, ελυμηνατο αυτην (Sept.). Austin understands it of Vespasian, others of Antiochus, or Antichrist.
paragraphs.anchor: The boar out of the wood

paragraphs.text: The soldiers, 2Ch 25:18.
paragraphs.anchor: And the wild beast

paragraphs.text: Some understand it of Christ’s incarnation, Luk 1:78.
paragraphs.anchor: Visit this vine

paragraphs.anchor: They perish

paragraphs.text: i.e. Israel, or the Messiah.

paragraphs.text: A promise of gratitude, which is usually annexed to prayers for deliverance.
paragraphs.anchor: So will not we go back

paragraphs.text: See Psa 80:7. Prayers are like arrows of deliverance, which would be multiplied and enlarged, 2Ki 13:17.
